title: Boost Mobile $300 Pre-Paid SIM Starter Kit for $265 Delivered @ Boost Mobile
body:
Deal: Boost Mobile $300 Pre-Paid SIM Starter Kit for $265 Delivered @ Boost Mobile

[Cho0028] For those who have Costco membership, I would say that Costco has the better deal for this. $250 plus the $30 Costco Gift Card puts it at $220 which is $45 cheaper. The savings of $45 essentially pays for the Costco membership in that instance.
[richplatt] I can't see any SIM deal on the Costco website at the moment. Is it store specific?
[mrhorse] This deal is more or less the same after the $45 cashback: $265 - 45 = $220
[sparky347] Absolutely - mine was an "information" post - not a "this is a better deal" post. I'm sure there are others like me who just CBF with cash/shopback :)
[Homr] 100%, I'd rather go with the auditech than to worry about saving $18 on shopback which might not even work!!
[whypaymo] All good, just thought I mention incase that was missed.
[PR0r] I'm needing 2, what's the best way to buy and get cashback for both?
[YpeKiYay] dont combine the transactions, purchase separately, see instructions
[sparky347] ….and…. Nobody should ever "recharge" these annual SIMs. I flip-flop between Telstra & Boost every year using a discount starter kit. You can buy in advance as long as the starter kit doesn't expire. I bought from Auditech a cuppla weeks ago for $230. My Telstra doesn't expire til mid November, so I'll miss the bonus data. But having used 27GB out of 300GB in 10 months - I think I'll scrape by
[thestig] Was just looking into this now but currently on Boost. Telstra on Auditech seems to be $285 for 165GB of data. Given I use around 200GB per year it doesn't seem to be worth the $15 saving by not just recharging for $300 on Boost unless I'm missing something?
[ozhunter68] The idea is the only port away for a short time using a low cost sim for 1 day to 30 days depaending on which sim
pack you can get cheap. Then just port back to your new 365 day boost sim pack of choice. Easy done.
[sparky347] Yeah, unforch, the $285/165GB is the old Telstra plan - they have to honour already circulating SIMs until 2/11 and as a disincentive there's no bonus activation data. Consider switching to Telstra for up to 7 days - which will cost $15, then activate a new (possibly Auditech $238) Boost SIM and get the 290GB.
General word of warning - when porting, don't do it in the evening, or on a Friday or weekend. First thing in the morning is best, Justin Case of any hiccups
[radnom] thanks, I tried to get optus for $199 yesterday: i got all the way through to payment and it failed. I was annoyed… but I guess they wanted me to go to boost instead.
[sickaunt] What does ‘full Telstra prepaid mobile network mean?
Is it just the Telstra wholesale network or does Boost now use full Telstra mobile network?
[ozhunter68] More than the Telstra wholesale network, still bit shy of the top Telstra tiers for full data speeds. Some will differ on here.
[kizzaaa] This does a good job explaining the coverage difference: https://www.whistleout.com.au/MobilePhones/Guides/Telstra-ne…
tldr: retail vs wholesale network mainly differs in rural/remote areas. speed caps can also apply to wholesale.
[sparky347] my 2c again - there is NO geographical difference between Telstra coverage and Boost coverage. There are some differences between Boost (which is only prepaid) and Telstra postpaid plans - data caps, QoS, smartwatch cellular. But there is ZERO difference between Boost and Telstra PREPAID services - the $74/28 day recharges on both have uncapped data speed
[jughead101] for cashback does it needs to be activated by a certain date of purchase or by Nov?
[monchee] I’ve now got the iPhobe Air. How do i go port out and then in with boost?
